title: File creation never routes through a here-string payload
question: Does the toolchain create files via a write API rather than a shell here-string, so a document quoting a destructive command is not scanned as one, and @' / '@ sequences round-trip? PASS requires a byte-exact round trip of a document containing both terminators.
answer: Yes. tools/lib/codex-invocation.mjs writeFileViaApi landed the document byte-exact (sha256=a1c4f408f8e2a7c820b37f1dc89345df6f8e81e88c7c5ac635b45bd12c82b427). The same bytes inlined into a Set-Content here-string terminated early on '@ and left Remove-Item / rm -rf in command text, so a command scanner fired. Static scan of tools/lib/ found 0 here-string file-creation sites.
execution_substrate: linux-local (PowerShell here-string semantics emulated; payload-scanned-as-command measured on constructed command text)
